(Surat al-Nur is Madani, and it has sixty-four verses.)

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿A surah﴾: that is, this is a surah, or [it is] a surah among what We have revealed to you. ﴿We sent it down﴾: this is its attribute (ṣifa). Whoever reads it in the accusative makes it an explanation (mufassir) of its governing verb, so it has no place in i'rab except when one estimates "recite" (utlu) or "[take] it as your own" (dūnaka) or the like before it. ﴿And We made it obligatory﴾: and We made obligatory what is in it of rulings. Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read it with the doubled letter (shaddadahu), either because of the abundance of its obligations (fara'id) or [because of] the obligated persons (al-mafrud 'alayhim), or for emphasis in making them binding. ﴿And We sent down in it clear verses﴾: clear in their indication. ﴿That you may remember﴾: so that you may avoid what is forbidden. It has also been read with the lightening of the dhal.

The fornicatress and the fornicator: [flog] whatever We have enjoined or sent down as their ruling, which is flogging. It is permissible for both to be in the nominative as the subject (mubtada'), with the predicate (khabar): ﴿So flog each one of them a hundred lashes﴾. The fa' (fa) is there because the subject carries the meaning of a conditional, since the lam (al-) is in the sense of alladhi ("the one who"). It has also been read in the accusative, with a verb implied that is explained by the apparent one; this is better than making surah ("a surah") an accusative for the sake of the command. And al-zani (the fornicator) is read without the yā' (ya). He placed al-zaniyah first because fornication in most cases occurs through her exposing herself to the man and offering herself to him; and because its corruption is realized through its attribution to her.

Al-jald (flogging) is striking the skin, and it is a ruling specific to one who is not muhsan (married/protected). This is because of what indicates that the punishment of the muhsan is stoning (rajm). Al-Shafi'i added to it the exile of a free person for one year, based on his saying, upon him be blessings and peace: "The virgin for the virgin: a hundred lashes and a year's exile." Nothing in the verse rules this out, so that one of them abrogates the other, abrogation being either accepted or rejected. For the slave there are three opinions.

Ihsan (protected status) is by freedom, puberty, sanity, and having had intercourse within a valid marriage. The Hanafis also required Islam, but this is rejected by his stoning two Jews, upon him be blessings and peace. And it is not contradicted by "Whoever associates partners with God is not muhsan," since the muhsan intended is the one for whom retaliation is taken from a Muslim.

﴿And let not pity for them take hold of you﴾: compassion (ra'fah: mercy). ﴿In the religion of God﴾: in His obedience and in establishing His legal limit (hadd), lest you suspend it or be lenient regarding it. For this reason he, upon him be blessings and peace, said: "Were Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, to steal, I would cut off her hand."

And Ibn Kathir read it with a fatha on the hamzah, and it has been read with a madd, in the form fa''alah.

﴿If you are believers in God and the Last Day﴾: for faith requires earnestness in obeying God Most High and striving in establishing His limits and rulings; and this is by way of stirring up (motivation). ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾: as an increase in deterrence, for public disgrace may deter more than physical punishment does. The word ṭā'ifah (group) means a company that can be gathered around something, such as a circle of people around a fire-spot; its least number is three, and it has been said one or two. The intended meaning is a gathering by which exposure is achieved.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 3:

﴿The fornicator does not marry except a fornicatress or an idolatress, and the fornicatress—none marries her except a fornicator or an idolater.﴾ Since, generally, the one inclined to fornication (p-99)

does not desire to marry the virtuous, and the fornicatress is not desired by the righteous. For similarity is a cause of affection and union, while difference is a cause of aversion and separation. The correct parallel construction would have been: "and the fornicatress does not marry except one who is a fornicator or an idolater." But the intent is to explain the condition of men in their desire for them, because the verse was revealed concerning the weaker among the Emigrants (al-Muhajirun) when they intended to marry prostitutes (baghaya) who would hire out themselves so that they might spend on them from their earnings, according to the custom of the Jahiliyyah. For this reason the fornicator was mentioned first. ﴿And that was made unlawful for the believers﴾ because it is an imitation of the wicked (fussaq) and an exposure to suspicion and a cause of evil talk and of slander against lineage, and other corruptions. For this reason, mere disapproval (tanzih) was expressed by the term prohibition (tahrim), for emphasis. It has also been said that the negation carries the meaning of a prohibition, and it has been read in that way; and the prohibition is to be taken in its literal sense, and the ruling is restricted to the occasion of revelation in which it came, or it is abrogated by His saying: ﴿And marry the single among you﴾, for it encompasses the fornicatresses. This is supported by the fact that he, upon him be blessings and peace, was asked about this and said: "Its beginning is fornication and its end is marriage, and the unlawful does not make the lawful unlawful." It has also been said that the intended meaning of "marriage" (nikah) is sexual intercourse (wat'), so it is interpreted as a prohibition on the fornicator from fornicating except with a fornicatress, and on the fornicatress that a fornicator should fornicate with her except with a fornicator—and this is corrupt.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (*Anwar al-Tanzil*) on surah 24, verses 4–5:

﴿And those who accuse chaste women﴾ (yarmuna al-muhsanat): they accuse them of fornication (al-zina), describing the accused women as chaste (muhsanat, "chaste," meaning free, adult, sane, Muslim, and abstaining from fornication). He mentions them after the fornicators and the requirement of four witnesses, by His saying: ﴿Then, if they do not bring four witnesses, lash them eighty lashes﴾. Slander (qadhf, false accusation of unlawful sexual intercourse) with other than this, such as saying "O sinner!" or "O wine-drinker!", requires discretionary punishment (ta'zir), like the slander of a woman who is not chaste. Ihsan (chastity, here meaning the conditions of the accused) is by freedom, puberty, sanity, Islam, and chastity from fornication, and there is no difference in this between males and females. The specification of "chaste women" is either because of the particular incident or because the slander of women is more common and more heinous. It is not required that the witnesses be present together at the time of testimony, and the testimony of the husband of the accused woman is not accepted, contrary to Abu Hanifa. Its lashing should be lighter than the lashing for fornication, because its cause is weaker and admits of doubt, and for this reason its number was reduced.

﴿And do not accept their testimony﴾ of any kind whatsoever, because he is a slanderer. It has been said that it refers to their testimony in slander. This does not depend on the completion of the lashing, contrary to Abu Hanifa, for the command to lash and the prohibition against accepting testimony are equal in being the answer to the condition, with no sequence between them, so both are consequent upon it at once. Moreover, his state before the lashing is worse than after it.

﴿Ever﴾ (abadan), as long as he does not repent. According to Abu Hanifa, it lasts until the end of his life.

﴿And those are the depraved﴾: those who have been judged to be depraved.

﴿Except those who repent﴾ of the slander, ﴿after that and make amends﴾: they amend their deeds by making reparation, which includes submitting to the prescribed punishment (hadd) or seeking the pardon of the accused. The exception (al-istithna') refers to the original ruling, which is the requirement of the condition for these matters. It does not necessarily follow that the prescribed punishment falls by it, as has been said, because submitting to it or seeking pardon is part of the completeness of repentance. The grammatical position of the exceptive element (mahalluhu) is the accusative (al-nasb) by way of exception. It has been said that it refers to the prohibition (al-nahy), and its position is the genitive (al-jarr) by way of substitution (al-badal) for the pronoun "hum" in "lahum." It has been said that it refers to the last clause, and its position is the accusative because it is from an affirmed statement (min mujib). It has also been said that it is a disjunctive exception (munqati') and a connected one (muttasil) with what follows.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving, Most Merciful﴾: this is the reason (illah) for the exception.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 6–7:

﴿And those who accuse their wives, and have no witnesses except themselves﴾ It was revealed concerning Hilal ibn Umayya, who saw a man on his wife's bed. "Anfusuhum" is either a substitute (badal) for "shuhada'" or a qualifier (sifah) of it, on the basis that "illa" here means "ghayr" (other than). ﴿Then the testimony of one of them is four testimonies﴾ That is, it is obligatory that the testimony of one of them be [four testimonies], or upon them is the testimony of one of them. "Arba'" is in the accusative as an infinitive (masdar), though Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs read it in the nominative, taking it as the predicate (khabar) of "shahadah". ﴿by Allah﴾ is connected to "shahadat" because it is nearer, and it is said it is connected to "shahadah" because of its precedence. ﴿Indeed he is of the truthful﴾ that is, in what he accuses her of regarding adultery. Its original form was "annahu" (that he), so the preposition was dropped and "inna" was made with a kasrah, and the governing verb was suspended from it by the lam for emphasis.(p-100)

﴿And the fifth﴾ and the fifth testimony. ﴿That the curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars﴾ in this accusation. This is the li'an (mutual imprecation) of the husband, and its ruling is the falling away of the hadd punishment for slander from him, and separation between the two occurs by itself, a separation of annulment (faskh) according to us, based on his saying, peace be upon him (ﷺ): "Those who perform li'an may never come together again." The separation by the judge is a divorce separation according to Abu Hanifah; the denial of the child requires that it be presented to him in this regard, and the establishment of the hadd punishment for adultery upon the woman, based on his saying.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 8–10:

﴿And it will avert from her the punishment﴾, that is, the hadd (the prescribed legal punishment). ﴿That she testify four testimonies by Allah that he is surely among the liars﴾ concerning what he has accused her of.

﴿And the fifth [testimony] that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is among the truthful﴾ concerning that. The fifth is in the nominative by the inchoative (al-ibtida'), and what follows it is the predicate (al-khabar), or it is in the conjunctive position, coordinated with ﴿that she testify﴾. Hafs read it in the accusative, coordinated with ﴿four﴾. Nafi' and Ya'qub read ﴿that the curse of Allah﴾ and ﴿that the wrath of Allah﴾ with the nun lightened in both, the dad in the kasra, the ba' in the fatha of "ghadiba", and the ha' of the name of Allah in the damma. The rest read with the nun in shadda in both, the ta' in the nasb, the dad in the fatha, and the ha' in the jarr.

﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Accepting of repentance and Wise﴾: the response (jawab) is omitted for magnification, meaning: surely He would have exposed you and hastened to punish you.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 11:

﴿Indeed, those who brought the slander (al-ifk)﴾ with the most eloquent form of lying. From al-ifk, which is "turning away" (al-sarf), because it is a statement turned away (ma'fuk) from its proper direction. The intended reference is to the slander that was fabricated against ʿA'isha, may Allah be pleased with her. The background is that the Prophet ﷺ took her along on one of the campaigns, and one night he gave permission to set out on the return journey. She walked off to attend to a need, then came back to the riding-saddle (rahl) and touched her chest, and found that her necklace of Zafar onyx (jaz' zafar) had broken. So she went back to look for it. Meanwhile, the man who used to load her onto the camel assumed she had entered the howdah, so he loaded it onto her mount and set off. When she returned to her place, she found no one there, so she sat down, expecting that someone would come back for her. Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal al-Sulami, may Allah be pleased with him, had stayed behind the army. He set out at night and arrived at her place at dawn. He recognized her, made his mount kneel, and she mounted it, and he led it until they reached the army. She was then accused because of him.

﴿A group among you﴾: a company from among you. It consists of ten to forty, and likewise the ʿisaba (band). He means ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, Zayd ibn Rifa'a, Hassan ibn Thabit, Mistah ibn Uthatha, Hamna bint Jahsh, and those who supported them. It is the predicate of inna. And His saying: ﴿Do not consider it bad for you﴾ is a new sentence (musta'naf), and the address is to the Messenger ﷺ, Abu Bakr, ʿA'isha, and Safwan, may Allah be pleased with them all, while the pronoun (ha') refers to the slander. ﴿Rather, it is good for you﴾, because by it you gain great reward and the manifestation of your honour before Allah, through the sending down of eighteen verses concerning your innocence, the magnifying of your status, the terrifying of the threat against whoever spoke about you, and the praise of those who thought well of you. ﴿For every man among them is what he earned of sin﴾: for each, there is a recompense for what he earned, in proportion to what he took part in, each individually. ﴿And the one who took upon himself the greater part of it﴾: its major portion. Yaʿqub read it with a ḍamma (kibruhu), and it is a dialect form of the same word. ﴿Among them﴾: among those who plunged into it. This is ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, for he initiated it and spread it out of enmity toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Or it refers to him, Hassan, and Mistah, for they supported him by openly speaking of it. And alladhi here means alladhina. ﴿For him is a great punishment﴾ in the Hereafter, or in this world, by being flogged; Ibn Ubayy became an outcast, famously known for hypocrisy, Hassan became blind with both hands paralysed, and Mistah became blind.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verses 12–13:

﴿Why did not﴾ (lawla, "why not", "would that") [when you heard it] ﴿the believing men and the believing women think good of their own kind﴾, meaning: of those among the believers, men and women, who are of them, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and do not defame one another﴾. He shifted in it from the second person address to the third person, for emphasis in rebuke and to signal that faith requires thinking well of the believers, refraining from attacking them, and defending them against those who attack them, just as they would defend themselves.

The separation between lawla (ﻟَوْلا) and its verb by the adverbial phrase is permissible because the adverbial phrase is treated as if it were the verb itself, inasmuch as it is never detached from it; and this latitude is allowed here in a way that is not allowed elsewhere. This is because mentioning the adverbial phrase is more important, since the urging is to ensure that they do not neglect its beginning. ﴿And say: "This is a manifest lie."﴾ as one who is certain and acquainted with the situation would say.

﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it? So when they did not bring the witnesses, then those are, in the sight of God, the liars.﴾ This is part of what was said, as confirmation that it is a lie, since whatever has no proof for it is a lie in the sight of God, that is, in His judgment; and for this reason He ordained the prescribed punishment upon it.

**Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on Surah 24, verses 14–15**

﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter﴾. *Lawla* (a particle meaning that one thing is not realized because another thing exists) here is for the non-occurrence of the consequence owing to the grace. The meaning is: were it not for the grace of Allah upon you in this world, through various kinds of blessings, among which is granting you respite for repentance, and His mercy in the Hereafter, through pardon and forgiveness, which are decreed for you. ﴿would have touched you﴾ immediately. ﴿for that which you plunged into﴾, that is, which you immersed yourselves in. ﴿a tremendous punishment﴾, before which the reproach and the flogging are considered trivial.

﴿When﴾ is an adverbial complement (*zarf*) modifying either ﴿would have touched you﴾ or ﴿you plunged into﴾. ﴿You received it with your tongues﴾: some of you take it from others by asking about it. One says *talaqqa al-qawl* ("he received the speech"), like *talaqquf* and *talaqqun* of it. It was read as *tatalaqqawnahu* in its original form; *talaqqawnahu* from *laqiyahu*, meaning he caught it; *tilqawnahu* with the vowel of the present-tense prefix (*harf al-mudara'a*) being kasra; *talaqqawnahu* from throwing it (*ilqa'ihi*) among one another; and *talaqqawnahu* and *ta'lqawnahu* from *al-alq* and *al-alaq*, which means falsehood; and *taqfunahu* from *thaqiftuhu*, meaning when I sought it and found it; and *taqfunahu*, that is, you follow it.

﴿And say with your mouths﴾, that is, and you say words that are confined to the mouths, without any support from the hearts. ﴿what you have no knowledge of﴾, because it is not an expression of knowledge of it in your hearts, like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts﴾.

﴿And you think it is trivial﴾, easy, with no consequence. ﴿while it is, in the sight of Allah, tremendous﴾ in burden and in drawing down punishment. Thus these are three sins arranged in sequence, to which the touching of the tremendous punishment is attached: receiving the falsehood with their tongues, speaking of it without verification, and their considering it insignificant, while it is, in the sight of Allah, tremendous.

It was read as *tatalaqqawnahu* in its original form; *talaqqawnahu* from *laqiyahu*, meaning he caught it; *tilqawnahu* with the vowel of the present-tense prefix (*harf al-mudara'a*) being kasra; *talaqqawnahu* from throwing it (*ilqa'ihi*) among one another; and *talaqqawnahu* and *ta'lqawnahu* from *al-alq* and *al-alaq*, which means falsehood; and *taqfunahu* from *thaqiftuhu*, meaning when I sought it and found it; and *taqfunahu*, that is, you follow it.

﴿And say with your mouths﴾, that is, and you say words that are confined to the mouths, without any support from the hearts. ﴿what you have no knowledge of﴾, because it is not an expression of knowledge of it in your hearts, like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts﴾.

﴿And you think it is trivial﴾, easy, with no consequence. ﴿while it is, in the sight of Allah, tremendous﴾ in burden and in drawing down punishment. Thus these are three sins arranged in sequence, to which the touching of the tremendous punishment is attached: receiving the falsehood with their tongues, speaking of it without verification, and their considering it insignificant, while it is, in the sight of Allah, tremendous.

﴿And why, when you heard it, did you not say, "It is not for us"﴾: that is, it is not proper for us, nor is it fitting for us. ﴿to speak of this﴾. The demonstrative may refer to the specific statement, or to its kind, since slandering ordinary people is forbidden by the Sharia, let alone attacking al-Siddiqa (the Truthful One), the daughter of al-Siddiq (Abu Bakr), and the sanctity of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). ﴿Glory be to You﴾ expresses amazement at that slander or at the one who says it. Its original use is to be said at every occasion of amazement, as a declaration of God's transcendence above anything being difficult for Him, and it later became common usage for every expression of amazement. Or it is a declaration of God's transcendence above allowing the sanctity of His Prophet to be defiled with immorality, since a wife's immorality repels people and undermines the purpose of marriage, unlike her disbelief. Thus it confirms what precedes it and paves the way for His words: ﴿This is a monstrous slander﴾, because of the greatness of the one against whom the slander is made, for the lightness or gravity of sins is measured by what they relate to.

﴿God admonishes you not to return to the like of this﴾: that is, lest you return to it, or regarding returning to it. ﴿Ever﴾: as long as you are alive and legally accountable (mukallafin, i.e., those bound by religious obligations). ﴿if you are believers﴾: for faith prevents one from it, and the phrase carries an incitement and a rebuke.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verses 19–20:

﴿Indeed, those who love﴾ (i.e., wish) ﴿that indecency should spread﴾ (i.e., be broadcast) ﴿among those who believe, for them is a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter﴾ — by the prescribed penalty (al-hadd) and the Blaze, and other than that. ﴿And Allah knows﴾ what is in the hearts. ﴿And you know not.﴾ So punish in this world according to what the apparent evidence indicates, while Allah, glorified is He, punishes for what is in the hearts of the love of spreading [gossip] (al-isha'a).

﴿And if not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy﴾ — this is a repetition of the favour by deferring punishment hastily, to indicate the enormity of the offence. For this reason He joined His statement ﴿and that Allah is Kind and Merciful﴾ to the occurrence of His bounty and mercy upon them. The response (jawab) is omitted, as it is dispensed with by its mention once before.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verses 19–20:

﴿Indeed, those who love﴾ (i.e., wish) ﴿that indecency should spread﴾ (i.e., be broadcast) ﴿among those who believe, for them is a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter﴾ — by the prescribed penalty (al-hadd) and the Blaze, and other than that. ﴿And Allah knows﴾ what is in the hearts. ﴿And you know not.﴾ So punish in this world according to what the apparent evidence indicates, while Allah, glorified is He, punishes for what is in the hearts of the love of spreading [gossip] (al-isha'a).

﴿And if not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy﴾ — this is a repetition of the favour by deferring punishment hastily, to indicate the enormity of the offence. For this reason He joined His statement ﴿and that Allah is Kind and Merciful﴾ to the occurrence of His bounty and mercy upon them. The response (jawab) is omitted, as it is dispensed with by its mention once before.

O you who have believed, do not follow the footsteps (khutuwat, plural of khutwa: step, path) of Satan. [By spreading the vile deed.] It is also read with the vowel of the ta' opened (khutawat), while Nafi', al-Bazzi, Abu 'Amr, Abu Bakr and Hamzah read it with the ta' sukun (khutuwat). "And whoever follows the footsteps of Satan, indeed he enjoins what is shameful and wrong." This explains the reason for the prohibition against following him. Al-Fahsha' (indecency, shamefulness) is that whose ugliness is extreme, and al-Munkar (what is wrong, denounced) is what the Sharia has denounced. "And if not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy," by granting the repentance that erases sins and the legislation of the prescribed punishments (hudud) that expiate them, "none of you would ever have been purified (ma zaka)," meaning would never have been cleansed of their filth. "From anyone, ever," meaning for all time. "But Allah purifies whom He wills," by guiding him to repentance and accepting it. "And Allah is Hearing," of what they say, "Knowing," of their intentions.

﴿And let them not swear﴾: let them not take an oath. It is from *ifti'al* (the eighth verbal form, a reflexive or reciprocal pattern) of *al-alyah* (oath). Alternatively, it means "let them not fall short" or "let them not neglect," from *al-alw* (falling short). The first meaning is supported by the variant reading *wa-la yata'alla* (with the verb in the form *yata'alla*).

It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), who had sworn that he would no longer spend on Mistah, who was the son of his maternal aunt and was one of the poor among the Emigrants. ﴿Those of virtue among you﴾: in religion. ﴿And of plenty﴾: in wealth. This indicates the excellence and nobility of Abu Bakr (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him).

﴿That they should give﴾: meaning "that they should not give," or "regarding giving." It is also read with a *ta'* (*tu'tu*), as a shift in grammatical person (*iltifat*, a change from third person to second person address). ﴿To the near of kin, the needy, and the emigrants in the way of Allah﴾: these are descriptions of one referent, meaning people who combine these qualities, since the discussion concerns those who are such; or they are descriptions of distinct referents placed in the position of one, which makes the justification of the intended meaning more emphatic.

﴿And let them pardon﴾: for what has passed from them. ﴿And let them overlook﴾: by disregarding it. ﴿Do you not love that Allah should forgive you?﴾: in return for your pardon, your forbearance, and your kindness toward one who has wronged you. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾: together with His complete power. So adopt His attributes.

It is narrated that he (ﷺ) recited it to Abu Bakr (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him), and he said: "Yes, I love (that)," and he restored his maintenance to Mistah.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verses 23–25:

.(p-103)

﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste women, who are unaware and believing,﴾ — "chaste" meaning the virtuous (al-ʿafaʾif). "Unaware" meaning unaware of what they are accused of. "Believing" meaning believing in Allah and His Messenger, [the accusation being made] to violate their honour and to slander the Messenger, peace be upon him, and the believers, as Ibn Ubayy did. ﴿They are cursed in this world and the Hereafter﴾ because they slandered them. ﴿And theirs is a great punishment﴾ due to the greatness of their sins. It is said that this is the ruling for every slanderer who does not repent. It is also said that it is specific to those who slandered the wives of the Prophet ﷺ; for this reason Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: "There is no repentance for him. If you searched through the threats of the Qur'an, you would not find anything more severe than what was revealed concerning the slander of ʿAʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her."

﴿On the day when their tongues, their hands and their feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do﴾ — this is a temporal clause (ẓarf) governing the sense of stability implied in "theirs" (lahum), not "punishment" (ʿadhab), since the latter is qualified. Ḥamzah and al-Kisaʾi read it with the ya' (yashhadu), on account of the intervening feminine plural noun and the separation. ﴿Their tongues, their hands and their feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do﴾ — they will acknowledge them by Allah's making these speak against their will, or through the manifestation of the effects of their deeds upon them. In this there is further intensification of the punishment.

﴿On that day Allah will pay them their due recompense in full (dīnahum al-ḥaqq)﴾ — their deserved reward. ﴿And they will know﴾ because they witness the matter directly. ﴿That Allah is the Manifest Truth (al-Ḥaqq al-Mubīn)﴾ — the One who is established in His essence, whose divinity is evident, with none sharing Him in that, and none able to grant reward or punishment besides Him; or, He is the Possessor of clear truth, i.e., the Just whose justice is manifest, and whoever has this attribute will certainly avenge the wronged against the wrongdoer.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 26:

﴿Evil women are for evil men, and evil men for evil women; good women are for good men, and good men for good women.﴾ That is: the evil (khaba'ith) women marry the evil (khabath) men and vice versa, and likewise the people of goodness. This serves as evidence for His saying: ﴿Those﴾, meaning the People of the House of the Prophet ﷺ, or the Messenger, 'Aisha and Safwan, may Allah be pleased with them all. ﴿are cleared of what they say﴾. For if it had been true, she would not have been his wife, peace be upon him, and he would not have been left with her. It has also been said that the evil and good [words] are among the sayings, and the reference to "the good ones" [is to] the saying of the slanderers. The pronoun in ﴿they say﴾ refers to the slanderers, meaning: they are cleared of what the slanderers say about them; or it refers to the evil men and evil women, meaning: they are cleared of saying the like of what they said. ﴿For them is forgiveness and a generous provision﴾, meaning Paradise. Allah has indeed cleared four people by four things: He cleared Yusuf, peace be upon him, by a witness from among her own family; Musa, peace and blessings be upon him, from the claim of the Jews about him, by the stone that went off with his garment; Maryam by making her child speak; and 'Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, by these noble verses, together with this emphasis. This was only to manifest the station of the Messenger ﷺ and to elevate his rank.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 27:

﴿O you who have believed, do not enter houses other than your houses﴾ in which you do not dwell, for the lessee and the lender also may not enter except with permission. ﴿Until you seek permission [yastaʾnisu] and greet their occupants﴾ — "tastaʾnisū" means "tastaʾdhinū," that you seek permission. It may be derived from al-istiʾnas (seeking familiarity) in the sense of al-istiʿlam (seeking information), from anasa al-shayʾ when he perceived it (ānasa al-shayʾa idhā abṣarahu), since the one seeking permission is seeking to know the situation and to uncover whether his entry is desired or whether he will be given leave. Or it is derived from al-istiʾnas, which is the opposite of al-istiḥashah (feeling of estrangement), since the one seeking permission feels estranged and fears that he will not be given leave; so when he is given leave, he becomes at ease (fa-idhā lahu istaʾnasa). Or [it means] that you make yourselves known, whether there is a human being (insān) of mankind (al-ins) there. ﴿And greet its occupants﴾ by saying: "Peace be upon you, may I enter?"

And from him, upon him be prayers and peace: "Greeting is that one says: 'Peace be upon you, may I enter?' three times. If he is given leave, he enters; otherwise he returns."

﴿That is better for you﴾ — i.e., seeking permission or greeting is better for you than entering suddenly, or better than the greeting of the Jahiliyyah, when a man among them entered a house other than his own, he would say: "May you be greeted in the morning" or "May you be greeted in the evening," and would enter, and perhaps he would come upon a man with his wife under a single covering.

It is narrated that a man said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Shall I seek permission to enter upon my mother?" He said: "Yes." He said: "She has no servant other than me; shall I seek permission to enter upon her every time I enter?" He said: "Would you like to see her naked?" They said: "No." He said: "Then seek permission."

﴿So that you may remember﴾ — this is connected to an omitted element, i.e., "It was sent down to you," or "This was said to you, with the intention that you remember" (p-104)

and act upon what is more beneficial for you.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verses 28–29:

﴿And if you find no one therein﴾ [who gives you permission]. ﴿then do not enter them until permission is given to you﴾ until someone comes who gives you permission. For the one who prevents entry is not merely the looking upon private parts (ʿawrat), but also what people customarily conceal, together with the fact that disposing of another's property without his permission is forbidden. He excepted the case where there is a fire or a flood in it, or where it contains something objectionable and the like. ﴿And if it is said to you, "Go back," then go back﴾ and do not insist. ﴿It is purer for you﴾ returning is cleaner for you from what insisting and standing at the door cannot avoid, namely displeasure and the neglect of good manners; or it is more beneficial for your religion and your worldly affairs. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of what you do﴾ so He knows what you do and what you leave undone of that which you have been addressed with, and He will requite you for it. ﴿There is no blame upon you for entering houses not inhabited⁠—﴾ such as hostels (ribat), shops (hawanit), inns (khanat), and khanqahs. ﴿wherein is provision for you﴾ enjoyment (istimtaʿ). ﴿for you﴾ such as shelter from heat and cold, storing goods, and sitting for transactions. This is an exception to the preceding ruling, since it covers both inhabited and uninhabited houses. ﴿And Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal﴾ a warning to whoever enters a place for corruption or for spying upon private matters.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 30:

﴿Tell the believing men to lower their gaze﴾, i.e., from whatever is forbidden (muharram) to look at. ﴿And guard their private parts﴾, except from their wives or what their right hands possess. Since the exception is like a rare, anomalous case, unlike lowering the gaze, he stated it absolutely and restricted the lowering of the gaze with the particle of partitive (ba'd, "some of"). It has also been said that guarding the private parts here specifically means covering them. ﴿That is purer for them﴾, i.e., more beneficial for them, or more purifying, because of what it entails of distance from suspicion (rayba).

﴿Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what they do﴾. Nothing is hidden from Him: the roving of their eyes, the use of their other senses, the movement of their limbs, and what they intend by them. So let them be wary of Him in every movement and stillness.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (*Anwar al-Tanzil*) on surah 24, verse 31:

﴿And say to the believing women that they should lower their gaze﴾, so that they do not look at what it is not lawful for them to look upon from men.

﴿And guard their private parts﴾, by concealing them or by protecting them from fornication (*zina*, unlawful sexual intercourse). The lowering of the gaze is mentioned first because looking is a pathway (*barid*, a messenger or precursor) to fornication. ﴿And not display their adornment﴾, such as jewelry, clothing and cosmetics, let alone the places of these adornments, to those to whom it is not lawful for them to display them. ﴿Except what appears of it﴾, in the course of handling things, such as clothing and the ring, for concealing these would cause hardship. It has been said that the meaning of "adornment" here is its places, with an elided noun (*hadhf al-mudaf*, the omission of a genitive noun), or that it encompasses both natural beauty and artificial adornment. The exception is the face and the two palms, because they are not *'awrah* (the parts of the body that must be covered). The more apparent view is that this ruling concerns prayer and not looking, for the whole body of a free woman is *'awrah*, and it is not lawful for anyone other than a husband or a non-marriageable kinsman (*mahram*) to look at any part of it, except out of necessity, such as medical treatment and giving testimony.

﴿And let them draw their head-coverings (*khumur*, sing. *khimar*, a veil) over their chests﴾, to cover their necks. Nafi', 'Asim, Abu 'Amr and Hisham read *juyubihinna* with a *damma* on the *jim*. ﴿And not display their adornment﴾: he repeated it to clarify who may be allowed to see it and who may not. ﴿Except to their husbands﴾, for they are the ones for whom adornment is intended, and they may look at the whole of her body, even the private part, though this is disliked. ﴿Or their fathers, or the fathers of their husbands, or their sons, or the sons of their husbands, or their brothers, or the sons of their brothers, or the sons of their sisters﴾, because of the frequency of their entering upon them, the women's need for their entry, and the scarcity of fear of temptation from them, since human nature has an aversion to intimacy with close relatives. They may look at what appears of the women while working and serving. The paternal and maternal uncles are not mentioned, either because they are in the position of brothers, or because it is more cautious for women to veil themselves from them, lest they describe them to their own sons. ﴿Or their women﴾, meaning the believing women, for unbelieving women do not refrain from describing them to men or to women in general, and the scholars differ on this. ﴿Or those whom their right hands possess﴾, which includes female slaves and male slaves, on the basis of what is reported: "The Prophet (ﷺ) came to Fatimah with a slave whom he had given to her, and she was wearing a garment which, when she covered her head with it, did not reach her feet, and when she covered her feet, did not reach her head. So the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'There is no harm for you; he is only your father and your servant.'" It has also been said that the intended meaning is female slaves only, and that a woman's male slave is like a non-kinsman with respect to her.

﴿Or male attendants who have no physical desire﴾, that is, men who have no need of women, namely the impotent elderly and the castrated (*mamsuhun*). Opinions differ concerning the one who has been castrated by cutting (*majbub*) and the eunuch (*khasi*). It has been said that they are the simpletons who follow people for the sake of their food and know nothing of women's affairs. Ibn 'Amir and Abu Bakr read *ghayri* in the accusative as a circumstantial state (*hal*). ﴿Or children who have not yet become aware of women's private matters﴾, because they have not reached the age of discernment, the word *zhuhur* here meaning "awareness" (*ittila'*); or because they have not reached the limit of sexual desire, the word *zhuhur* here meaning "dominance" (*ghalaba*). *Tifl* (child) is a singular noun used in the place of the plural, sufficient because of the indication of the qualifying description.

﴿And let them not stamp their feet so that what they hide of their adornment may be known﴾, so that her anklet jingles and it becomes known that she wears an anklet, for this would arouse inclination in men. This is more emphatic than the prohibition against displaying adornment and more indicative of the prohibition against raising the voice.

﴿And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you, O believers﴾, for hardly does anyone among you escape negligence, especially in restraining oneself from desires. It has been said that it means: repent of what you used to do in the time of ignorance (*jahiliyyah*), for although it is wiped away by Islam, it is still obligatory to feel remorse for it and to resolve to refrain from it whenever it is remembered. Ibn 'Amir read *ayyuhal-mu'minun* ("O believers") and in *al-Zukhruf* (*ayyuhal-sahir*, "O sorcerer") and in *al-Rahman* (*ayyuhal-thaqalan*, "O two weighty ones") he read the *ha'* with a *damma* in connected speech in these three places, while the others read it with a *fatha*. Abu 'Amr and al-Kisa'i paused on them with the *alif*, while the others paused without the *alif*.

﴿So that you may succeed﴾, with the happiness of both abodes.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 32:

﴿And marry off the unmarried among you, and the righteous among your male and female slaves.﴾ When He forbade what might lead to fornication (sifah), which undermines lineage and which calls for mutual affection, good upbringing, and increased compassion, leading to the preservation of the species, He forbade it emphatically, and then followed it with the command of marriage (nikah), which protects against it. The address is to the guardians (awliya') and masters (sadah). In it there is evidence for the obligation of marrying off the woman under guardianship and the slave, and that is upon their request. It also indicates that a woman and a slave may not independently conclude it, for if they could, it would not be obligatory upon the guardian and the master. "Ayama" (أيامى) is a metathesis of "ayaymu," like "yatama" (orphans), the plural of "ayyim," which is the unmarried, whether male or female, virgin or previously married. He said:

"So if you marry, I will marry, and if you remain unmarried, [I too will remain unmarried], even though I am more worthy of marriage than you, I am remaining unmarried."

The specification of the righteous is because preserving their religion and attending to their affairs is more important. It is said that the intended meaning is those who are fit for marriage and capable of fulfilling its rights. ﴿If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty.﴾ This is a rebuttal of what might prevent marriage. The meaning is: the poverty of the suitor or the betrothed should not prevent marriage, for in Allah's bounty there is sufficiency from wealth, since it comes and goes. Alternatively, it is a promise from Allah of enrichment, based on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Seek wealth through this verse." However, it is conditional upon His will, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will soon enrich you from His bounty, if He wills.﴾ ﴿And Allah is All-Encompassing⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠—﴾ possessor of vastness whose blessing never runs out, since His power has no end. ﴿All-Knowing⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠—﴾ who extends provision and determines what His wisdom requires.(p-106)

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 33:

﴿And let those who find no means of marriage keep themselves chaste﴾ — let them strive for chastity and for suppressing desire. ﴿Those who find no means of marriage﴾ — its causes (asbab). It is also permissible that by "marriage" is meant that by which one marries (i.e., the means of marriage), or that by "finding" is meant being able to access it. ﴿Until Allah enriches them of His bounty﴾ — so that they find what they may marry with.

﴿And those who seek a writing (kitab)﴾ — the contract of emancipation (mukatabah), which is that a man says to his slave, "I have made a contract of emancipation with you for such-and-such, from the kitab," because the master has written upon himself the manumission of the slave once he pays the money; or because it is something that is written, for its deferment; or from kataba meaning "to gather," because the consideration in it is paid in installments, with some joined to others. ﴿Of those whom your right hands possess﴾ — whether a male slave or a female slave. The relative clause with its complement is the subject (mubtada'), whose predicate is ﴿then make a contract with them﴾; or it is an object of a suppressed verb whose explanation is this. The fa' (then) is for the implication of the meaning of a condition. The command in it is for recommendation (nadb) according to most scholars, because mukatabah is a exchange contract that includes kindness, so it is not obligatory, like other such contracts. The argument of the Hanafis from its absolute wording for the permissibility of an immediate mukatabah is weak, because the absolute does not generalize, and moreover inability to pay at present prevents its validity, as in salam (advance sale) regarding what is not available at the time of due date. ﴿If you know in them good﴾ — trustworthiness and capability to pay the money through earning a trade. A similar statement has been transmitted as a marfu' (attributed to the Prophet) report. It was also said: righteousness in religion. It was also said: wealth. Its weakness is apparent in both wording and meaning, and it is the condition of the command, so the absence of the condition does not necessitate the absence of permissibility.

﴿And give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾ — a command to the masters, as in what precedes it, that they should give them some of their wealth; and in its meaning is remitting some of the mukatabah money. It is obligatory according to most scholars, and the least amount that counts as property suffices.

It is related from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that he would remit a quarter, and from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, a third. It was also said that it is a recommendation to them to spend on them after they have paid and been freed. It was also said that it is a command to the general body of Muslims to assist the mukatabs and to give them their share from zakat; and it is permissible for the master, even if he is wealthy, because he does not take it as charity, like the creditor and the buyer. This is indicated by the words of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in the hadith of Barirah: "It is a charity for her and a gift for us."

﴿And do not compel your slave girls﴾ — your female slaves. ﴿To prostitution﴾ — to fornication. "Abdullah ibn Ubayy had six slave girls whom he compelled to fornication and imposed taxes upon them. Some of them complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so this was revealed." ﴿If they desire chastity﴾ — seeking to remain chaste — is a condition for the compulsion, for it does not exist without it. If it is made a condition for the prohibition, the absence of it does not necessitate the permissibility of compulsion, because the lifting of the prohibition may be by the abstention from what is forbidden. The choice of "in" (in) over "idha" (when) is because the desire of chastity among slave girls is like the rare and anomalous case. ﴿That you may seek the goods of the worldly life. And whoever compels them, then indeed Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ — i.e., to them, or to him if he repents. The first is more suitable to the apparent meaning, and to what is in the codex of Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him: "after their compulsion, for them, is Forgiving and Merciful." It is not objected that the compelled woman is not sinful, so there is no need for forgiveness, because compulsion does not negate accountability in itself; for this reason compulsion makes killing forbidden for the one compelled, and makes retaliation obligatory upon him.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 34:

﴿And We have certainly sent down to you verses that make things clear﴾ He means the verses that were made clear in this surah and in which the rulings (ahkam) and punishments (hudud) were explained. Ibn 'Amir, Hafs, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read the word mubayyinat with a kasra (mubayyinat, rather than mubayyanat) in this place and in Surat al-Talaq, because the verses are clear (wadihat) and are confirmed by the earlier Scriptures and by sound reason. Here bayyana is used in the sense of tabayyana (to become clear). Or it is read this way because the verses have made the rulings and punishments clear. ﴿And an example from those who passed away before you﴾ Or, "and an example from the likes of those who came before you," meaning a wondrous story similar to their stories, namely the story of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, for it is like the story of Yusuf and Maryam. ﴿And an admonition for the God-fearing﴾ He means what was admonished in those verses. The God-fearing (muttaqin) are singled out because they are the ones who benefit from them. It has also been said that the "verses" refer to the Qur'an and the attributes mentioned in it are its attributes.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 35:

﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth.﴾ Light (nur), in its origin, is a quality that the eye perceives first, and through it all other visible things are perceived, like the quality emanating from the two luminaries (nayyirayn, i.e., the sun and the moon) onto the dense bodies facing them. In this sense, it cannot be applied to Allah, exalted is He, except by supposing an omitted genitive construction (mudaf), as in your saying: Zayd is generosity (karam), meaning: possessor of generosity. Or it is applied figuratively, either in the sense of "illuminator of the heavens and the earth," and it has been read this way, for He, exalted is He, illuminated them with the stars and what flows from them of lights, or with the angels and the prophets. Or [it means] "their governor," from the saying of people about a leader who excels in management: "the light of the people," because they are guided by him in affairs. Or [it means] "their originator," for light is manifest in itself and makes other things manifest, and the origin of manifestation is existence, just as the origin of concealment is non-existence, and Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, is existent in Himself and the originator of all besides Him. Or [it means] "that by which one perceives, or by which its people perceive," inasmuch as it is applied to the sight (basirah) because it is connected to it, or because it shares with it the dependence of perception upon it; then [it is applied] to the insight (basirah) because it is stronger in perception, for it perceives itself and others, of universals and particulars, existents and non-existents, and it plunges into their inner depths and manipulates them by composition and analysis. Then these perceptions are not essential to it, for otherwise they would not separate from it; so they are from a cause that bestows them upon it, and that is Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, either directly or through the mediation of the angels and the prophets. For this reason they were called lights. Close to this is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father: its meaning is "guide of those in them, so they are guided by His light." Its attribution to the heavens and the earth is either to indicate the breadth of its radiance, or because they contain sensible and intellectual lights, and because perceptions fall short of them, and of what is related to them and what signifies them.

﴿The likeness of His light﴾: the description of His light, which is of wondrous nature. Its attribution to His pronoun, glory be to Him and exalted, is evidence that its application to Him is not in its apparent sense.

﴿is like a niche﴾: like the description of a niche (mishkah), which is a non-penetrating recess in a wall. Al-Kisa'i, in the transmission of al-Duri, read it with imala (inclination of the vowel).

﴿wherein is a lamp﴾: a large, piercing lantern. It has been said that the mishkah is the tube in the middle of the lamp-stand, and the misbah is the burning wick.

﴿The lamp is in a glass﴾: in a lamp-stand made of glass.

﴿The glass is as if it were a shining star﴾: luminous, sparkling, like Venus in its clarity. Its name (durri) is derived from al-dar' (repelling), and the form fu'ayyil, like murayq, from al-dar', for it repels darkness with its light; or some of its light repels some of its shine. Its hamza was changed into ya'; and the reading of Hamza and Abu Bakr upholds the original form, while the reading of Abu 'Amr and al-Kisa'i "dirri'" (like shirrib) is also read in reversed form.

﴿kindled from a blessed tree, an olive, ﴾: that is, the origin of the lamp's flame is from an olive tree whose benefit is abundant, in that its wick is nourished by its oil. The indefiniteness of the tree, its description with blessing, and then the substitution of "olive" for it, is an exaltation of its status. Nafi', Ibn 'Amir and Hafs read with the ya' and the passive form from awqada; Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr read with the ta' likewise, on attributing it to "the glass," with an omitted genitive. It has been read "tawaqqadu" from tatawaqqadu, and "yuqadu" with the ta' omitted for the accumulation of two additions, and this is rare.

﴿neither of the east nor of the west﴾: it is not struck by the sun from time to time, but rather in such a way that the sun strikes it all day long, like one that grows on a hill, or in a wide plain, for its fruit is then more ripe and its oil purer; or it is not growing in the east or the west of the inhabited world but in its middle, which is Syria, for its olive is the finest of olives; or it is not in a place of sunrise where the sun constantly shines upon it and scorches it, nor in a place of setting where the sun constantly leaves it, so it leaves it unripe. In a hadith: "There is no good in a tree or a plant in a place of setting, nor is there good in either of them in a place of sunrise."

﴿Its oil would almost glow even if no fire touched it﴾: that is, its oil would almost shine by itself without fire, due to its brilliance and its intense gleam.

﴿Light upon light﴾: a multiplied light, for the light of the lamp was increased in brightness by the purity of the oil, the splendor of the lamp-stand and the containment of the niche for its rays. Several aspects have been mentioned concerning the meaning of the parable. The first: it is a parable of the guidance indicated by the clear verses, in the clarity of their meaning and the manifestation of the guidance they contain, by the described niche. Or it is a comparison of guidance, inasmuch as it is surrounded by the darkness of people's illusions and imaginings, to the lamp; and the kaf (like) only governs the niche because it contains the lamp, and its comparison to it is more fitting than its comparison to the sun. Or it is a parable of what Allah illuminated in the heart of the believer of knowledge and sciences, by the light of the niche spread within it from its lamp, and this is supported by the reading of Ubayy: "The likeness of the light of the believer." Or it is a parable of what Allah granted His servants of the five ordered perceptive faculties upon which livelihood and the hereafter depend, namely: the sensory faculty, by which sensible things are perceived through the five senses; the imaginative faculty, which preserves the forms of those sensible things so as to present them to the intellectual faculty whenever it wishes; the rational faculty, which perceives universal realities; the cogitative faculty, which composes intelligibles in order to deduce from them knowledge of what was not known; and the holy faculty (al-quwwah al-qudsiyyah), in which the flashes of the unseen and the secrets of the divine realm are manifested, specific to the prophets and the saints, which is what is meant by His saying, exalted is He:

﴿But We made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants﴾: by the five things mentioned in the verse, namely: "the niche," "the glass," "the lamp," "the tree," and "the oil." The sensory faculty is like the niche, for its locus is like a recess, its face is turned to the outside, it does not perceive what is behind it, and its illumination is through intelligibles, not essentially. The imaginative faculty is like the glass in accepting the forms of perceived things from all sides and preserving them for the intellectual lights, and in illuminating them with what it contains of intelligibles. The rational faculty is like the lamp, for it is illuminated by universal perceptions and divine knowledge. The cogitative faculty is like the blessed tree, for it leads to fruits without end, the olive bearing oil, which is the material of lamps, which are neither of the east nor of the west, for they are free of corporeal attachments; or because they lie between forms and meanings, acting upon both categories and benefiting from both sides. The holy faculty is like the oil, for by its purity and intense acuity it almost shines with knowledge without reflection or learning. Or it is a parable of the rational faculty in its stages through this: at the beginning of its affair it is empty of sciences, prepared to receive them like the niche; then it is engraved with necessary sciences through the mediation of the sense perception of particulars, to the point where it is able to attain theoretical knowledge, and it becomes like the glass, shining in itself, receptive to lights. That attainment, if it is by thought and effort, is like the olive tree; if by intuition, like the oil; and if by a holy faculty, like that whose oil almost glows, for it almost knows even without contact with the angel of revelation and inspiration, whose likeness is fire inasmuch as intellects are kindled by it. Then, once knowledge has been acquired by it to the degree that it can summon it whenever it wishes, it is like the lamp; and when it summons it, it is light upon light.

﴿Allah guides to His light﴾: to this piercing light. ﴿whom He wills﴾: for causes are futile without His will, since by it they are completed.

﴿And Allah strikes parables for mankind﴾: bringing the intelligible near to the sensible, by way of clarification and explanation. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing of everything﴾: whether intelligible or sensible, manifest or hidden. In this there is a promise and a warning for whoever reflects upon them, and for whoever pays them no heed.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 36–38:

﴿In houses﴾ is connected to what precedes it, meaning: (the light is) like a niche in some houses, or: it is lit in some houses. In this case the restriction applies to the thing used as the likeness, with a description that conveys its elevation and emphasis, for the lamps of the mosques are greater. Or it is an illustration of the prayers of the believers, or of their bodies, by the mosques. The plurality of "houses" does not contradict the singularity of "niche," since what is meant is whatever has this description, without regard to unity or plurality. Or it is connected to what follows, "He is glorified," and there is an emphatic repetition in it, which is not a problem because it belongs to the complement of "that," so it does not govern what precedes it. Or it is connected to an omitted verb, such as "They glorify (Him) in houses." What is meant by the houses is the mosques, because the attribute suits them. It has been said that the mosques are the three (sacred mosques), and the indefiniteness is for magnification. ﴿God has permitted﴾ that it be raised, by building or by exalting it. ﴿And that His name be mentioned therein﴾ is general, covering everything that its mention includes, even the discussion of His acts and the investigation of His rulings. ﴿Therein He is glorified morning and evening by men﴾, that is, they exalt Him, meaning they pray to Him therein in the mornings and evenings. "Morning" (al-ghuduww) is a verbal noun used for the time, and for this reason its pairing with "evenings" (al-asal) is apt; al-asal is the plural of asil. It has been read "wa-l-iyṣal," which is entering the evening. Ibn 'Amir and Abu Bakr read "yusabbah" with a fatḥa, on the basis of its being attributed to one of the three adverbs of time, with "men" in the nominative as indicated by it. It has also been read "tusabbih" with a kasra, due to the feminine plural, and with a fatḥa, on the basis of its being attributed to the times of morning.

﴿Men whom neither trade nor sale diverts﴾ means: a profitable transaction does not occupy them. ﴿From the remembrance of God﴾ is an emphasis by generalization after specification, if by it is meant any kind of distraction, or by singling out what is most important of the two kinds of trade, for profit is realized through selling and anticipated through buying. It has been said that trade here means buying, since it is its root and origin. It has been said that it means importing, since that is most prevalent in it, and from this one says "tajara fi kadha" when one imports such-and-such, and this implies that they are merchants. ﴿And the establishment of prayer﴾: the genitive is substituted here for the ta' of compensation in place of the omitted 'ayn through the inflection, as in his saying:

"And they broke with you the promise which they had made."

﴿And the giving of zakat﴾ is what must be paid out of wealth to those entitled to it. ﴿They fear a day﴾ together with what they are upon of remembrance and obedience. ﴿In which hearts and eyes will be turned about﴾: they will be agitated and change from terror, or their states will be transformed, so hearts comprehend what they did not comprehend and eyes see what they did not see; or hearts turn between hope of salvation and fear of destruction, and eyes (turn) toward whichever side they are seized from and whence their record is given.

﴿That God may reward them﴾ is connected to "He is glorified," or to "neither trade nor sale diverts," or to "they fear." ﴿The best of what they did﴾: the best reward for what they did, the paradise promised to them. ﴿And increase them of His bounty﴾: things He did not promise them in return for their deeds, and which did not occur to their minds. ﴿And God provides for whom He wills without reckoning﴾ is an affirmation of the increase and an alert to the perfection of power, the execution of will, and the vastness of grace.

Ibn 'Amir and Abu Bakr read "yusabbah" with a fatḥa, on the basis of its being attributed to one of the three adverbs of time, with "men" in the nominative as indicated by it. It has also been read "tusabbih" with a kasra, due to the feminine plural, and with a fatḥa, on the basis of its being attributed to the times of morning.

﴿Men whom neither trade nor sale diverts﴾ means: a profitable transaction does not occupy them. ﴿From the remembrance of God﴾ is an emphasis by generalization after specification, if by it is meant any kind of distraction, or by singling out what is most important of the two kinds of trade, for profit is realized through selling and anticipated through buying. It has been said that trade here means buying, since it is its root and origin. It has been said that it means importing, since that is most prevalent in it, and from this one says "tajara fi kadha" when one imports such-and-such, and this implies that they are merchants. ﴿And the establishment of prayer﴾: the genitive is substituted here for the ta' of compensation in place of the omitted 'ayn through the inflection, as in his saying:

"And they broke with you the promise which they had made."

﴿And the giving of zakat﴾ is what must be paid out of wealth to those entitled to it. ﴿They fear a day﴾ together with what they are upon of remembrance and obedience. ﴿In which hearts and eyes will be turned about﴾: they will be agitated and change from terror, or their states will be transformed, so hearts comprehend what they did not comprehend and eyes see what they did not see; or hearts turn between hope of salvation and fear of destruction, and eyes (turn) toward whichever side they are seized from and whence their record is given.

﴿That God may reward them﴾ is connected to "He is glorified," or to "neither trade nor sale diverts," or to "they fear." ﴿The best of what they did﴾: the best reward for what they did, the paradise promised to them. ﴿And increase them of His bounty﴾: things He did not promise them in return for their deeds, and which did not occur to their minds. ﴿And God provides for whom He wills without reckoning﴾ is an affirmation of the increase and an alert to the perfection of power, the execution of will, and the vastness of grace.

The Qur'an, 24:39: "And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain (qay'ah)..."

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil)

﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain﴾. And the state of those who disbelieve is the opposite of that. Their deeds, which they consider to be righteous and beneficial in the sight of Allah, they will find to be vain and frustrating in the outcome, like the mirage. The mirage is what is seen in the desert at midday, from the shining of the sun upon it, so that one thinks it is water flowing (yasrubu), that is, running. The qay'ah means the qa' (the flat, open ground), which is the land empty of vegetation and other things, level. It was said that its plural is like jar and jirah, and it was read as "biqay'at" like dimat in dimah.

﴿The thirsty one thinks it is water﴾, that is, the parched one. Its specification is to liken the disbeliever to it in the intensity of disappointment at the moment of greatest need.

﴿Until, when he comes to it﴾: what he imagined to be water, or its place, comes to him.

﴿He finds it to be nothing﴾ of what he supposed.

﴿And finds Allah with him﴾: His punishment, or His guardians of Hell (zabaniyah), or he finds Him calling him to account.

﴿So He pays him his due reckoning﴾, by reviewing it or by recompensing him.

﴿And Allah is swift in reckoning﴾: He is not occupied by one reckoning from another.

It is narrated that it was revealed concerning Utbah ibn Rabi'ah ibn Umayyah, who was devout in the pre-Islamic period and sought the religion, but when Islam came, he disbelieved.

﴿Or like darknesses﴾ is coordinated with (like a mirage). The particle (or) here is for choice (*takhyīr*). Their deeds, because they are futile and have no benefit, are like the mirage. And because they are empty of the light of truth, they are like the darknesses piled up in the depths of the sea, the waves, and the clouds. Or the particle is for classification (*tanwīʿ*): if their deeds are good, they are like the mirage, and if they are ugly, they are like the darknesses. Or it is for division (*taqsīm*) according to two times: they are like darknesses in this world and like the mirage in the Hereafter.

﴿In a deep sea﴾: possessing *lujj*, that is, deep. It is a relative noun derived from *al-lujj*, which is the greater part of the water.

﴿Covers it﴾: it covers the sea. ﴿A wave above it, a wave﴾: that is, successive waves piled one upon another. ﴿Above it﴾: above the second wave.

﴿Clouds﴾: they covered the stars and blocked their light. The clause is another description of (sea). ﴿Darknesses﴾: that is, these are darknesses.

﴿Some of them above others﴾. Ibn Kathir read ﴿darknesses﴾ with the *kasra* (genitive), either as a substitution for the first (darknesses) or by the annexation of (clouds) to it, according to the transmission of al-Bazzi.

﴿When he brings out his hand﴾, and this is the nearest that can be seen of it. ﴿He almost cannot see it﴾: he was not near to seeing it, let alone seeing it clearly, like the saying of Dhu al-Rummah:

*When distance alters the lovers, the trace of love for Mayya scarcely departs from the heart of passion.*

The pronouns refer to the one who is in the sea, even though it has not been mentioned, because the meaning points to it.

﴿And whoever Allah does not give light﴾, and whoever He does not decree guidance for, and does not grant success to its causes. ﴿Then for him there is no light﴾: unlike the one who is granted success, for whom there is light upon light.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verses 41–42:

﴿Have you not seen﴾ (alam tara): Have you not known with a knowledge that resembles direct observation in certainty and firmness, whether by revelation (wahy) or by inference (istidlal)? ﴿that Allah is glorified by whoever is in the heavens and the earth﴾: the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth declare Him free of every deficiency and defect, the one who declares Him free of them being the one who is in them. The word ﴿whoever﴾ (man) is used to give precedence to rational beings (al-'uqala'), or to the angels and the two weighty ones (al-thaqalan, i.e. jinn and humans), through what indicates this, whether by speech (maqal) or by the indication of a state (dalalat hal). ﴿And the birds﴾: on the first reading, this is a specification of what they contain of manifest craftsmanship (sun') and striking proof (dalil), and for this reason He qualified them with His words ﴿in flight﴾ (saffat). For giving heavy bodies that by which they are able to stand in the air, spreading their wings, along with what is in them of folding and spreading, is a decisive proof of the perfect power of the Maker (al-Sani') and the subtlety of His governance.

﴿Each﴾ (kull): each one of what has been mentioned, or each of the birds. ﴿has indeed known its prayer and its glorification﴾: that is, Allah has indeed known its supplication and its declaration of His purity, whether by choice or by nature, in accordance with His words ﴿and Allah is Knowing of what they do﴾. Or each one knows (its own prayer and glorification) in the manner of a likeness of its state in indicating the truth and inclining toward what benefits, in a way that is specific to the state of the one who knows this. Yet it is not far-fetched that Allah, exalted is He, inspires the birds with supplication and glorification, just as He inspired them with subtle knowledge concerning the means by which they sustain their lives, which rational beings can scarcely come to know. ﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾: for He is the Creator of both and of what is in them of essences, attributes and actions, insofar as these are contingent (mumkinah) and must end in the Necessary Being (al-Wajib). ﴿And to Allah is the final return﴾: the return of all.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 43:

﴿Have you not seen that Allah drives along the clouds﴾ means He drives them along. From this comes the expression "al-biḍā'ah al-muzjāh" (the meagre merchandise), for everyone drives it along. ﴿Then He joins them together﴾ by making them scattered fragments, so that He gathers some of them to others. On this basis, "baynahu" (between them) is correct, since the meaning is "between its parts." Nafi', according to the narration of Warsh, read "yu'allifu" without hamza. ﴿Then He makes it heaped up﴾ piled, some of it upon others. ﴿Then you see the rain﴾ the rain ﴿coming out from within it﴾ from its openings; "khilal" is the plural of "khalal," like "jibal" for "jabal." It is also read "min khalalihi" (from its openings). ﴿And He sends down from the sky﴾ from the clouds; everything above you is called "sama'" (sky). ﴿mountains in it﴾ masses of large pieces resembling mountains in their size or their hardness. ﴿of hail﴾ is an explanation of "mountains," and the object is omitted, meaning "He sends down" as a beginning ﴿from the sky, mountains in it of hail﴾, hail. It is permissible that the second or third "min" be partitive, standing in the position of the object. It has been said that what is meant by "sky" is the canopy, and that in it are mountains of hail, just as on earth there are mountains of stone; nothing in reason prevents this. The well-known view is that when vapours rise and are not dissolved by heat, they reach the cold layer of the air, and when the cold there intensifies, they gather and become cloud. If the cold is not intense, they fall as rain in drops. If it is intense, then if it reaches the vaporous particles before they gather, it falls as snow; otherwise it falls as hail. Sometimes the air becomes extremely cold, contracts and condenses into cloud, from which rain or snow falls. All of this must be traced back to the will of the Necessary, Wise Being, since there is proof that this will is what makes events specific to their places and times. He alluded to this with His words: ﴿So He strikes with it whom He wills and averts it from whom He wills﴾, where the pronoun refers to "barad" (hail). ﴿The flash of its lightning nearly takes away the sight﴾ the light of its lightning. It is read with a long vowel, meaning "height," and with the "d" assimilated into the "s," as "wa-buraqahu," with a damma on the "b" and a fatha on the "r," which is the plural of "burqah," a measure of lightning, like "ghurfah"; and with damma for the sake of harmony. ﴿It nearly takes away the sight﴾ the sight of those who look at it, because of the intensity of its brightness. This is the strongest proof of the perfection of His power, in that it brings forth the opposite from the opposite. It is also read "yadhhabu" with an added "ba'."

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verses 44–45:

﴿Allah alternates the night and the day.﴾ This is by succession between them, or by the decrease of one and the increase of the other, or by the change of their conditions through heat and cold, darkness and light, or by what encompasses all of that. ﴿Indeed in that﴾ — that is, in what has been mentioned before — ﴿is a lesson for those of vision.﴾ It is a proof of the existence of the eternal Creator, of the perfection of His power, the comprehensiveness of His knowledge, the effectiveness of His will, and His transcendence above need and whatever leads to need, for those who reflect with insight.

﴿And Allah created every creature﴾ — every animal that crawls upon the earth. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "khaliqu kulla dabbah" (the Creator of every creature), with the genitive construction (idafah). ﴿From water﴾ — it is a part of its substance, or it is a specific water, namely the sperm-drop (nutfah), so that the majority is treated as the whole, since among animals there are those that come into being from a sperm-drop. It has also been said that ﴿from water﴾ is connected to "creature" (dabbah) and not to "created" (khalaqa). ﴿So among them is one that walks on its belly﴾ — like the snake. The crawling is called "walking" by way of metaphor (isti'arah) or by correspondence (mushakalah). ﴿And among them is one that walks on two legs﴾ — like humans and birds. ﴿And among them is one that walks on four﴾ — like cattle and wild beasts. This includes what has more than four, like spiders, since their support, when they walk, is on four. The pronoun is masculine in agreement with the predominance of rational beings (taghlib al-'uqala'), and the expression "among them" (man) is used for the categories so that the detail corresponds to the general statement, and the order follows the precedence of what is more evident in power. ﴿Allah creates what He wills﴾ — of what has been mentioned and what has not been mentioned, simple and compound, with differences in forms, organs, shapes, movements, natures, faculties and actions, while the element is one, according to the requirement of His will. ﴿Indeed Allah is over all things Competent﴾ — so He does whatever He wills.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 46–48:

﴿We have indeed sent down clear signs﴾ (ayat mubayyinat), showing the realities (lil-haqa'iq) by means of various kinds of proofs. ﴿And Allah guides whom He wills﴾ by granting success (bi-l-tawfiq) in reflecting upon them (lil-nazar fiha) and pondering their meanings (wa-l-tadabbur li-ma'aniha). ﴿To a straight path﴾, which is the religion of Islam, the path that leads to attaining the truth and to success with Paradise.

﴿And they say, "We believe in Allah and in the Messenger"﴾. It was revealed concerning Bishr the hypocrite, who disputed with a Jew, and the Jew invited him to Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, while he (the Jew) was inviting him to the Prophet ﷺ. It was also said concerning Mughirah ibn Wa'il, who disputed with Ali (radiya Allahu 'anhu) over a piece of land, and he refused to have him judged by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. ﴿And we obey﴾, meaning, and we obey both of them. ﴿Then a faction of them turns away﴾ by refraining from accepting his judgment. ﴿After that﴾, after their saying this. ﴿But those are not believers﴾: the demonstrative refers to those who made the statement in its entirety, so this is an announcement from Allah, exalted is He, that all of them, even though they professed faith with their tongues, their hearts did not believe; or it refers to the faction among them, and faith is denied of them because of their turning away. The definite article in "al-mu'minin" indicates that they are not the believers you know, namely those who are sincere in faith and steadfast upon it.

﴿And when they are called to Allah and His Messenger, that he may judge between them﴾, meaning, that the Prophet ﷺ may judge, for he is the one who judges outwardly and the one called upon; Allah is mentioned to glorify Him and to indicate that his judgment ﷺ is in reality the judgment of Allah, exalted is He. ﴿Behold, a faction of them are averse﴾: a faction of them suddenly turned away when the right was against them, knowing that you would not judge in their favor. This is an explanation of "turning away" and an emphasis upon it.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verses 49–50:

﴿And if the right is theirs﴾, i.e., the judgment is in their favor and not against them, ﴿they come to him in submission﴾, obedient, because they know that he will rule in their favor. And (p-112)

("ilayhi," "to him") is connected either to "ya'tu" ("they come") or to "muðh'ininn" ("in submission"), and its being placed first is for exclusivity (ikhtisas).

﴿Is there a disease in their hearts﴾, i.e., disbelief or an inclination toward injustice? ﴿Or do they doubt﴾, by seeing from you some accusation, so that their certainty and their trust in you disappear?

﴿Or do they fear that Allah and His Messenger will wrong them﴾ in the judgment? ﴿Rather, they are the wrongdoers﴾. This is a turning away from the last two divisions in order to affirm the first division. The reasoning of the division is that their refusal is either due to a defect in them or in the judge. The second is either realized in their view or merely anticipated, and both are false, because the rank of his prophethood and his extreme trustworthiness ﷺ prevent it. So the first is established. Their wrongdoing encompasses the defect of their belief and the inclination of their souls toward injustice. And the separation (of the matter) is to negate that from others, especially the one who is called to his judgment.
