Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verses 51–52:

﴿The only saying of the believers, when they are called to Allah and His Messenger that He may judge between them, is that they say: "We hear and we obey." And those are the successful.﴾ This is in keeping with the practice of the Exalted in following the mention of the one who is right with the one who is wrong, and in drawing attention to what is fitting after denouncing what is not fitting. It is also read as "qawlu" (in the nominative) and "liyuhkama" (in the passive voice), with its subject being the pronoun referring to its source, meaning "that judgment may be carried out."

﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger﴾ in what they command him, or in the obligatory duties and the sunnas (recommended practices). ﴿And fears Allah﴾ for what has proceeded from him of sins. ﴿And keeps his duty to Him﴾ in the remainder of his life. Ya'qub and Qalun, on the authority of Nafi', read it without a ya' (yattaqhi becomes yattaqhu, with the ha' vowelled as a u-sound, i.e. "wa yattaqhu"), Abu Bakr and Abu 'Amr read it with the ha' sukun (quiescent), and Hafs read it with the qaf sukun, treating "taqhi" like "katif" (lightened), while the ha' is quiescent in pause by general agreement. ﴿Then those are the achievers﴾ of the everlasting bliss.

Ya'qub and Qalun, on the authority of Nafi', read it without a ya' (yattaqhi becomes yattaqhu, with the ha' vowelled as a u-sound, i.e. "wa yattaqhu"), Abu Bakr and Abu 'Amr read it with the ha' sukun (quiescent), and Hafs read it with the qaf sukun, treating "taqhi" like "katif" (lightened), while the ha' is quiescent in pause by general agreement. ﴿Then those are the achievers﴾ of the everlasting bliss.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verses 53–54:

﴿And they swore by God with their most solemn oaths﴾: a denial that they refrained from obeying his ruling. ﴿If you ordered them﴾ to leave their homes and their property, ﴿they would surely leave.﴾ The clause ﴿they would surely leave﴾ is the answer (jawab) to ﴿they swore﴾, given in direct quotation (hikaya, i.e. reporting their words as they said them). ﴿Say: Do not swear﴾ falsely. ﴿Obedience is known﴾: that is, what is required of you is known obedience, not oaths about hypocritical and reprehensible obedience. (Or: ﴿obedience is known﴾ is better than it, or let there be obedience.) It was also read in the accusative, ﴿ta'atun*﴾ as in "obey with obedience" (aṭī'ū ṭā'atan). ﴿Indeed God is well aware of what you do﴾, so your inner secrets are not hidden from him.

﴿Say: Obey God and obey the Messenger﴾: a command to convey what God addressed to them, in direct quotation, as an intensification of their rebuke. ﴿But if you turn away, then upon him﴾, that is, upon Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿is only what he has been charged with﴾ of conveying. ﴿And upon you is what you have been charged with﴾ of compliance. ﴿And if you obey him﴾ in his ruling, ﴿you will be guided﴾ to the truth. ﴿And upon the Messenger is only the clear conveyance﴾: the conveyance that makes clear what you have been obligated to. He has indeed fulfilled it. What remains is ﴿what you have been charged with﴾: if you fulfil it, it is for your benefit, and if you turn away, it is upon you.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 55:

﴿Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ This is addressed to the Messenger (ﷺ) and to the community (ummah) first of all, and to those who are with him. The word "min" (from) here is for explanation (li-l-bayan). ﴿That He will surely make them successors (yastakhlifannahum) in the earth﴾, that is, He will surely make them successors who exercise authority in the earth as kings exercise authority over their subjects. This is the answer to an implied oath, its implied sense being: Allah promised them and swore that He would surely make them successors. Or the promise, in its certainty, is treated as if it were an oath. ﴿As He made successors of those before them﴾, meaning the Children of Israel, whom He made successors in Egypt and the Levant after the tyrants. Abu Bakr read it with a damma on the ta' and a kasra on the lam (yustakhlifahum), and when he began a sentence he pronounced the alif with a damma; the rest read it with a fatha on both, and when they began a sentence they pronounced the alif with a kasra. ﴿And He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them﴾, namely Islam, by strengthening and firmly establishing it. ﴿And He will surely change their state after their fear﴾ from the enemies into security (amnan) for them. Ibn Kathir and Abu Bakr read it with the light form (al-takhfif). Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and his companions had remained in Makkah for ten years in fear, then they emigrated to Madinah, and they would begin the morning and end the evening carrying weapons, until Allah fulfilled His promise, making them victorious over all the Arabs and opening to them the lands of the East and the West. In this there is evidence for the truth of prophethood, since it reports the unseen as it is, and for the caliphate of the Rightly Guided Caliphs, since the one promised and the promise concerning it did not, by consensus (ijma'), come together for anyone other than them. It has been said that the fear is of punishment and the security from it is in the Hereafter.

﴿They worship Me﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) from "those," to restrict the promise to steadfastness upon monotheism; or it is a resumed statement explaining what necessitates the succession and security. ﴿Not associating anything with Me﴾ is a circumstantial clause from the waw, meaning: they worship Me without associating partners. ﴿And whoever disbelieves﴾, that is, apostatizes or disbelieves this blessing, ﴿after that﴾, such as after the promise or the attainment of the caliphate. ﴿Those are the defiantly disobedient (al-fasiqun)﴾, the complete ones in their defiance, since they apostatized after the clarity of verses like these, or they disbelieved that great blessing.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verses 56–57:

﴿And establish the prayer, and give the zakat, and obey the Messenger﴾ in all that he has commanded you. It is not far-fetched that this phrase is conjoined to ﴿obey God﴾, since the intervening element is a promise concerning what is commanded. In that case, the repetition of the command to obey the Messenger (ﷺ) is for emphasis. The attaching of mercy to obedience, or to what obedience is included in, is by His saying: ﴿so that you may receive mercy﴾, just as guidance was attached to it.

﴿Do not think that those who disbelieve will escape [Us] in the earth.﴾ Do not think, O Muhammad, that the disbelievers can escape God from His seizing them and destroying them. The phrase ﴿in the earth﴾ is a ṣila (a complement that completes the meaning of the word it is attached to) of ﴿escape﴾ (مُعْجِزِينَ).

Ibn ʿAmir and Hamza read it with the letter ya' (يَحْسَبَنَّ), on the basis that the pronoun in it refers to Muhammad (ﷺ). The meaning is the same as in the reading with ta' (تَحْسَبَنَّ). Alternatively, ﴿those who disbelieve﴾ is the subject (fāʿil), and the meaning is: let not the disbelievers think that anyone in the earth can escape God. Then ﴿escaping in the earth﴾ is the object pair. Or the meaning is: they do not think them (مُعْجِزِينَ). In that case, the first object is deleted, because the subject and the two objects refer to one thing, so the verb suffices with mentioning two of the three.

﴿And their abode is the Fire﴾ is conjoined to it in meaning, as if it were said: those who disbelieve are not able to escape, and their abode is the Fire. This is because the purpose of the prohibition against supposing is to establish the negation of escaping.

﴿And wretched is the destination﴾: the abode to which they go.

*Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 58:*

﴿O you who have believed, let those whom your right hands possess ask your permission﴾. This is a return to completing the rulings that preceded, after finishing with the divine matters (al-ilahiyyat) that indicate the obligation of obedience in the rulings that came before and others, the promise of reward for them, and the warning against turning away from them. What is meant is the address to men and women, with men given precedence in the address, because it is narrated that the slave of Asma' bint Abi Marthad entered upon her at a time she disliked, and so this was revealed.

It was also said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Mudlij ibn Amr al-Ansari, who was a boy, at the time of midday to summon Umar. He entered while [Umar] was sleeping and his garment had become uncovered. Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'I wish that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had forbidden our fathers, our sons and our servants from entering upon us at these times without permission.' Then he went with him to the Prophet (ﷺ) and found that this verse had been revealed."

﴿And those among you who have not reached puberty﴾: these are the children who have not reached puberty among the free. He expressed puberty by the wet dream (ihtilam), because it is its strongest sign.

﴿Three times﴾: in the day and night, once [each time].

﴿Before the dawn prayer﴾: because it is the time of rising from the beds, removing sleeping garments and putting on the clothes of wakefulness.

Its position (mahalluhu) is accusative as a substitute (badal) for "three times," or nominative as the predicate (khabar) of an omitted subject, i.e., "they are before the dawn prayer."

﴿And when you put off your clothes﴾: i.e., your clothes for wakefulness, for the midday rest (al-qaylula).

﴿From the noonday heat﴾: an explanation (bayan) of the time.

﴿And after the night prayer﴾: because it is the time of being stripped of clothing and of wrapping oneself in the covering.

﴿Three times of privacy (awrat) for you﴾: i.e., they are three times in which your concealment is disturbed. It is permissible that it be a subject (mubtada') whose predicate is what follows it. The root of 'awrah is a defect (khalal), and from it comes "a'war al-makan" (the place became exposed/defective) and "rajul a'war" (a man with a defective eye).

Abu Bakr, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read ﴿thalatha﴾ (three) in the accusative, as a substitute for ﴿thalatha marratin﴾ (three times).

﴿There is no sin upon you or upon them beyond these [times]﴾: beyond these times, in omitting seeking permission. There is nothing in it that contradicts the verse on seeking permission so as to abrogate it (fa-yansakhuha), because this [ruling] concerns children and the slaves of the one entered upon, whereas that [verse] concerns free adult believers.

﴿They are frequent attendants upon you﴾: i.e., they are those who go about among you. This is a resumption (istinaf) explaining the excuse that permits omitting permission, namely close association and frequent entering. In this is evidence for the rationale of rulings (ta'lil al-ahkam), and likewise for the distinction between these three times and others, by their being "awrat."

﴿Some of you upon others﴾: some of you circulate among others, or some of you go about to others.

﴿Thus﴾: like this explanation.

﴿Allah makes clear to you the verses﴾: i.e., the rulings.

﴿And Allah is Knowing﴾ of your conditions. ﴿Wise﴾ in what He has legislated for you.

**Commentary of al-Baydawi (*Anwar al-Tanzil*) on Surah 24, verses 59–60:**

﴿When the children among you reach puberty, let them ask permission, as those before them asked permission.﴾ "Those before them" refers to those who reached puberty before them, at all times. Those who held that a mature slave must ask permission of his master cited this verse as evidence. The reply is that the intended referents are the known persons (*al-ma'hudun*), who were made a category distinct from the slaves (*al-mamalik*), so they are not included among them. ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you His signs, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾ He repeated it for emphasis and to stress the command to ask permission.

﴿And women past child-bearing,﴾ meaning the old women who have ceased menstruating and bearing children. ﴿who have no hope of marriage,﴾ who do not expect it because of their old age. ﴿there is no blame upon them if they put aside their outer garments,﴾ that is, the outer garments such as the *jilbab*. The fa' here is because the *lam* in *al-qawa'id* carries the sense of *allati* (those who), or because the relative clause qualifies them with it. ﴿without displaying adornment.﴾ That is, without showing any adornment of the kind they were commanded to conceal, in His words: ﴿and not reveal their adornment﴾. The root of *tabarruj* (ostentatious display, "making a show of") is the affectation of revealing what is hidden, from the phrase *safina barija*, a ship with no covering on it. *Baraj* is the breadth of the eye such that its whiteness is seen surrounding all of its blackness without any of it hidden. It was specifically used for a woman uncovering her adornments and charms before men. ﴿But if they refrain, it is better for them,﴾ than putting them aside, because it is further from suspicion. ﴿And Allah is All-Hearing﴾ of their speech to men, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of their intention.

ليس على الأعمى حرج ولا على الأعرج حرج ولا على المريض حرج﴾ نفيٌ لِما كانوا يتحرّجون منه من مؤاكلة الأصحّاء، خوفًا من استقذارهم لهم، أو من أكلهم من بيت مَن يُدفع إليهم المفتاح ويُبيح لهم التبسّط فيه إذا خرج إلى الغزو وخلّفهم على المنازل، خشيةَ ألّا يكون ذلك من طيب قلب، أو من إجابة مَن دعوهم إلى

(p-115)

بيوت آبائهم وأولادهم وأقاربهم فيُطعمونهم كراهةَ أن يكونوا كلًّا عليهم. وهذا إنما يكون إذا عُلم رضا صاحب البيت بإذنٍ أو قرينةٍ، أو كان ذلك في أول الإسلام ثم نُسخ (أي رُفع حكمه، والنسخ: إبطال حكم سابق بحكم لاحق) بنحو قوله ﴿لا تدخلوا بيوت النبي إلا أن يُؤذن لكم إلى طعام﴾. وقيل: نفيٌ للحرج عنهم في القعود عن الجهاد، وهو لا يلائم ما قبله ولا ما بعده. ﴿ولا على أنفسكم أن تأكلوا من بيوتكم﴾ من البيوت التي فيها أزواجكم وعيالكم، فيدخل فيها بيوت الأولاد، لأن بيت الولد كبيته، لقوله عليه السلام: «أنت ومالُك لأبيك»، وقوله عليه السلام: «إن أطيبَ ما يأكل المؤمنُ من كسبه، وإنّ ولدَه من كسبه».

﴿أو بيوت آبائكم أو بيوت أمّهاتكم أو بيوت إخوانكم أو بيوت أخواتكم أو بيوت أعمامكم أو بيوت عمّاتكم أو بيوت أخوالكم أو بيوت خالاتكم أو ما ملكتم مفاتحه﴾ وهو ما يكون تحت أيديكم وتصرّفكم من ضيعةٍ أو ماشيةٍ، بالوكالة أو الحفظ. وقيل: بيوت المماليك. والمفاتح جمع مِفتَح، وهو ما يُفتح به، وقُرئ «مِفتاحَه». ﴿أو صديقكم﴾ أو بيوت صديقكم، فإنهم أرضى بالتبسّط في أموالهم وأُسَرُّ به، وهو يقع على الواحد والجمع كالخليط. هذا كلُّه إنما يكون إذا عُلم رضا صاحب البيت بإذنٍ أو قرينةٍ، ولذلك خُصّص هؤلاء، فإنه يُعتاد التبسّط بينهم، أو كان ذلك في أول الإسلام فنُسخ، فلا احتجاج للحنفية (أتباع المذهب الحنفي في الفقه) به على أنه لا قطعَ بسرقة مال المَحرَم. ﴿ليس عليكم جُناحٌ أن تأكلوا جميعًا أو أشتاتًا﴾ مجتمعين أو متفرّقين. نزلت في بني ليث بن عمرو من كنانة، كانوا يتحرّجون أن يأكل الرجل وحده. وقيل: نزلت في قومٍ من الأنصار، إذا نزل بهم ضيفٌ لا يأكلون إلّا معه. وقيل: في قومٍ تحرّجوا عن الاجتماع على الطعام لاختلاف الطبائع في القذارة والنَّهَمة. ﴿فإذا دخلتم بيوتًا﴾ من هذه البيوت ﴿فسلّموا على أنفسكم﴾ على أهلها الذين هم منكم دينًا وقرابةً. ﴿تحيّةً من عند الله﴾ ثابتةً بأمره، مشروعةً من لَدُنه. ويجوز أن تكون صفةً للتحية، فإنه طَلَبَ الحياةَ وهي من عنده تعالى، وانتصابها بالمصدر لأنها بمعنى التسليم. ﴿مباركةً﴾ لأنه يُرجى بها زيادةُ الخير والثواب. ﴿طيّبةً﴾ تطيب بها نفسُ المستمع.

وعن أنسٍ رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال لي: «متى لقيتَ أحدًا من أمّتي فسلّم عليه يَطُلْ عمرُك، وإذا دخلتَ بيتَك فسلّم عليهم يَكثُرْ خيرُ بيتك، وصلِّ صلاةَ الضحى فإنها صلاةُ الأبرارِ الأوّابين».

﴿كذلك يبيّن الله لكم الآيات﴾ كرّره ثلاثًا لمزيد التأكيد وتفخيم الأحكام المختتَمة به، وفصلُ الأولين بما هو المقتضى لذلك، وهذا بما هو المقصودُ منه، فقال: ﴿لعلكم تعقلون﴾، أي الحقَّ والخيرَ في الأمور.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 62:

﴿The believers are only those⦆ meaning those who are perfect in faith. ﴿who believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾ with the sincerity of their hearts. ﴿And when they are with him on a matter requiring assembly﴾ such as the Friday prayer (al-Jumu'ah), the festivals, wars, and consultation on affairs. The matter is described as requiring assembly for emphasis. It has also been read as "amrun jami'un" (a matter that gathers). ﴿they do not leave until they have asked his permission﴾ that is, they ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he grants them permission. Making this a condition of perfect faith is because it serves as the proof of its soundness and as the distinguishing mark of the sincere believer from the hypocrite, for the hypocrite's habit is stealing away and fleeing. It also magnifies the sin of leaving the gathering of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) without his permission. For this reason He repeated it, emphasizing it in a more eloquent style, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who ask your permission are those who believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾. This indicates that the one who asks permission is certainly a believer, and that leaving without permission is not so. ﴿So when they ask your permission for some of their affairs﴾ meaning the urgent matters that arise for them. This also contains emphasis and narrowing of the matter. ﴿grant permission to whomever you will among them﴾ this is a delegation of the matter to the opinion of the Messenger (ﷺ). It has been used as evidence that some rulings are delegated to his judgment. Those who prohibit this restrict the "will" to being subject to his knowledge of their truthfulness, so the meaning is: grant permission to whomever you know has an excuse. ﴿and ask Allah's forgiveness for them﴾ after the permission, for asking permission, even for an excuse, is a shortcoming, since it gives precedence to the affairs of this world over the affairs of religion. ﴿Indeed Allah is Forgiving﴾ of the lapses of His servants.(p-116)

﴿Merciful﴾ in facilitating matters for them.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 63:

﴿Do not make the calling of the Messenger among yourselves like the calling of some of you to others.﴾ Do not equate his calling you with the calling of one of you to another, in the permissibility of turning away from it, being lax in responding, and leaving without permission. For hastening to respond to him, peace be upon him, is obligatory, and departing without his permission is forbidden. It has also been said: do not make his calling and his naming like the calling of one of you to another by name, raising the voice with it, and calling from behind the apartments; rather, address him by his honorific title, such as "O Prophet of God" and "O Messenger of God", with reverence, humility and lowering of the voice. Or: do not make his supplication against you like the supplication of one of you against another, so do not disregard his anger, for his supplication is binding. Or: do not make his supplication to his Lord like the supplication of a child to his elder, who accepts it once and rejects it another time, for his supplication is answered.

﴿Indeed, Allah knows those who slip away from among you﴾ who slink away little by little from the congregation. The like of tasallal is tadarraja (to proceed gradually) and tadakhkhala (to slip in).

﴿covertly﴾ (liwadhan), a concealed slipping away, by one of you hiding behind another until he leaves, or by clinging to someone who has been given permission and going out with him as though he were his follower. Its position is as a circumstantial accusative (hal). It has also been read with a fatha on the lam.

﴿So let those who oppose his command beware﴾ who oppose his command by abandoning what it requires, and who take a course contrary to his course. The preposition ("an) is used because the verb includes the meaning of turning away. Or: they turn away from his command, apart from the believers, from one who opposes it by turning away from the command when he turns away from it, apart from him. The object is omitted because the intent is to specify the one who opposes and the one opposed; the pronoun refers to God, Exalted, since the command truly belongs to Him, or to the Messenger, since he is the one principally mentioned.

﴿lest a trial befall them﴾ a tribulation in this world.

﴿or a painful punishment befall them﴾ in the Hereafter. This has been cited as evidence that the command denotes obligation, for it indicates that abandoning what the command requires entails one of the two punishments, since the command to beware of it indicates fear of what is conditioned upon the existence of its cause, and that necessitates obligation.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 64:

﴿Indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. He already knows the state you are in﴾ — addressing those who are accountable — [whether it is] opposition or agreement, hypocrisy or sincerity. He emphasized His knowledge with "qad" (indeed/already) only to emphasize the warning. ﴿And the Day they are returned to Him﴾ — the Day the hypocrites are returned to Him for recompense. It is also permissible that the address is specifically directed at them, by way of iltifat (a shift in grammatical person, from direct address to third person or vice versa). Ya'qub recited it with a fatha on the ya' and a kasra on the jim (yurja'una, read as yarji'una with the first letter vowelled differently, so that the verb is active rather than passive).

﴿Then He will inform them of what they did﴾ of evil deeds, by rebuke and by recompense for it. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of all things﴾ — nothing concealed from Him is hidden.

From the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surah al-Nur will be given the reward of ten good deeds for each believing man and believing woman, in the past and in the future."
